title: Preventive use of cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) in the home care setting in LVAD patients to reduce driveline infections
summary:
Driveline infection (DLI) (an infection of the exit site of the driveline cable supplying the left ventricular assist device) is reported in the literature with an incidence of 20–40% following implantation of a left ventricular assist device (LVAD). These infections or wound-healing complications occur most frequently within the first 180 days after LVAD implantation, followed by a steady decline in the incidence of this complication.
The aim of this project is to determine the impact of the continuous and consistent preventive use of cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) on the occurrence of DLI.
First, the patient is informed about the project and written informed consent is obtained. In the clinic, dressing changes in these patients are additionally supplemented with the application of CAP twice weekly at the driveline exit site using the kINPen® MED device.
Prior to outpatient treatment, patients are randomly assigned to one of two treatment groups: Group 1 (without CAP) or Group 2 (with CAP).
In Group 1 (without CAP), treatment is performed according to standard care with regular visits by a wound care specialist.
In Group 2 (with CAP), in addition to the standardized procedure, CAP is additionally applied during dressing changes.
To ensure continuous use of CAP, patients are provided with a CAP device approved for home use and application by laypersons, including the corresponding accessories. Instruction in the use of the device is provided during the standardized training sessions and discharge preparation by the VAD coordination team. The CAP device used is PlasmaDerm®, manufactured by Cinogy GmbH.
Regardless of group allocation, the routinely scheduled LVAD follow-up visits are conducted according to the HDZ NRW standard outpatient schedule. The first follow-up takes place approximately 4–6 weeks after discharge to home care. Thereafter, quarterly outpatient follow-up visits are scheduled.
No additional examinations are performed.
The observation period begins with the first postoperative dressing change, which is performed by a VAD coordinator. The research study concludes one year later.
conditions: Infection and inflammatory reaction due to other cardiac and vascular devices, implants and grafts

interventions.name:
Rehabilitation and home care:
Standard dressing changes twice weekly performed by specialized wound care experts or by the patient/family; without CAP application.

Rehabilitation and home care:
Twice-weekly standard dressing changes performed by specialized wound care experts or by the patient/family, supplemented by the application of cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) as part of the standardized dressing change of the driveline exit site for a period of up to 12
